sentences.text: At the outset, it may be noted that Petitioners herein are inter alia successors in interest of one Harkesh.
Before filing of the present reference, as per record, another reference was decided U/S 30/31 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 vide award dated 17.01.2008 passed in LAC No. 123/2/06.

In the said reference, it was held that the LRs of Harkesh are entitled to receive entire compensation qua acquired land bearing Khasra No. 275/41-76 (8-12), 98 (4-6), 99 (2-18) and 107/1 (3-12) for a total area measuring 19 bighas and 8 biswa situated at Village Garhi Mendu as per their entitlement.
3. If one peruses the said award dated 17.01.2008, it transpires that Harkesh left behind 3 sons namely Rampal, Mange Ram, Brahm Singh; two daughters namely Rampali and Nandi; and wife Bhauti Devi.

4. Said Rampal, Mange Ram and Brahm Singh had expired at the time of deciding of the said reference and all their legal heirs had made statements before the Court deciding the above reference that they have relinquished their claim to receive compensation qua the acquired land in favour of respective wives of Rampal, Mange Ram and Brahm Singh.
5.
Similar statements were made by the other LRs of Harkesh namely his daughters Rampali and Nandi; and his wife Bhauti Devi.

6. In effect, as per the award dated 17.01.2008, only Bati wife of Mange Ram;
Bhagirathi wife of Brahm Singh; and Shaymo Devi wife of Rampal were held entitled to receive compensation qua the acquisition in question.
The said three individuals are the original petitioners before this Court.
7. I may note that Shaymo Devi died during pendency of this reference and her legal heirs were eventually taken on record.

8. The petitioners had approached the LAC for making a reference to this Court on the ground that the amount awarded qua the acquisition in question was much below the potential value of the land acquired and thus, they sought enhancement upto the rate of Rs. 20,000/- per sq yards.

9. On the other hand, LAC and DDA had objected to the said enhancement on the ground that the amount awarded for the acquisition was as per law and thus, they did not call for any interference by this Court.
10. As per the award of LAC dated 19.06.1992, for the village in question, the market value of the acquired land was assessed at Rs. 27,344/- per bigha.

The LAC awarded an additional amount @ 12% per annum on the said market value from the date of notification U/S 4 of the Act i.e. 23.06.1989 till the award i.e. 19.06.1992 [U/S 23 (1A) of the said Act]; and Solatium @ 30% on the market value [U/S 23 (2) of the said Bati And Others vs Uoi (Garh Mendu) on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85039796/
3 Act].

sentences.text: This case alongwith a batch of petitions was decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide a common judgment.

In the said judgment, the award in question i.e. Ex. R1/X Award No. 13/92-93 dated 19.06.1992 for Village Garhi Maindu inter alia fell for consideration and while deciding the said appeal, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has ordered that for the said Village i.e. Garhi Maindu @ Garhi Mendu shall also be entitled to the compensation at Rs. 2,07,500/- per bigha.

21. Vide the said judgment, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, after taking note of Section 28 A of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, has further held that "where in an Award the Court allows compensation to an applicant in respect of the acquired land, all persons whose land has been similarly acquired would be awarded, the same compensation, even if they had not applied for the same.
Once a particular rate of compensation is judicially determined, the benefit of such rate must be given to all persons whose land was acquired under the same Notification.

Thus, all persons whose land has been similarly acquired in these four Villages of Kilokari, Khirzabad, Nangli Razapur and Garhi Maindu shall also be entitled to the enhanced compensation."
22.
In the said judgment, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has allowed enhanced compensation with interest and all other statutory benefits in accordance with law.
23. Respondents before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the aforesaid case i.e. Union of India and DDA are respondents before this Court.

24. Counsel for the petitioners submitted that in view of the above judgment, now petitioners should be awarded enhanced compensation on the same lines as awarded by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the aforesaid case.
25. Petitioners herein have claimed compensation @ Rs. 20,000/- per sq yards.

But, save and except filing copies of some judgments passed in cases involving the same award, no sale deed or other documentary evidence was filed before this Court to reach a conclusion as to how the petitioners are entitled to compensation @ Rs. 20,000/- per sq yards.

9% per annum for the first year and @ 15% for subsequent years till making of payment by LAC i.e.
23.07.2004 as per provisions of Section 34 of LA Act
. 
(vi) The amount shall be apportioned into three equal sums with P-1 and P-2 taking equal shares and the third share being jointly paid to the LRs of P-3 brought on record.

Reference petition stands answered.
